Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Automatic loadout preferences

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Each staging picker now includes an automatic choice alongside loaded explicit choices. Skin and iron display By seat; Q/E display Auto. New profiles use all four automatic choices. Both directions traverse the automatic entry and skip catalog holes. Choosing any entry still clears readiness.

An automatic skin resolves from the current seat modulo the three skins. An automatic iron resolves from the seat's position in the current gun catalog, skipping an absent entry. Automatic abilities use the classic Q/E defaults (1/2), falling back to the first loaded ability if needed. Explicit choices remain fixed. Resolution happens before declaring a profile, so remote peers and the simulation receive ordinary concrete, validated IDs. No automatic sentinel enters gameplay.

The local profile codec now writes version-2 content 0x52535950524f4632. It adds four automatic-choice bits to the identity-bound record. The strict version-1 reader maps older records to explicit choices, preserving their stored profile, identity and epoch/tick. Merely decoding an old record does not modify its bytes; subsequent successful saving uses version 2. Undefined bits, corrupt envelopes and wrong identities are rejected. Automatic choices add no world/action/event or run-checkpoint fields; gameplay content changes are tracked separately.

Native atomic-file writes and browser revision-checked IndexedDB writes retain the existing durability rules. The mode is saved only when its resolved choices match authority, preventing an older acknowledgement from persisting a different explicit choice. The last confirmed mode supplies the recovery baseline. Initial UI baselines wait for the opening profile claim, and a generation change recognizes choices that were accepted in the same tick before applying that baseline. Choosing auto survives a fresh process and resolves again if that process gets another seat; choosing explicit then persists those IDs on later seats. With persistence disabled the modes apply only to the current session.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/automatic_run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/automatic_web_run.sh

Evidence covers model resolution/cycling, a frozen version-1 record, native/browser fresh-process and changed-seat checks, and profile corruption/write-conflict regressions. The browser fixture also verifies that another peer receives the resolved choices. The ability pickers now offer an explicit return to Auto; the original ability cycler only used its automatic fallback when it could not find a loaded row. Remaining presentation/platform work, playtests and full comparison remain open.
